provenance.pins: datasheet p.1 SOT-23 package drawing: 1 G, 2 S, 3 D

designVerdict: SELECTED as Q1,Q2 - the two FAULT interlocks, one per channel. No longer the PD follower: Q3 is now an MMBT5551 (C7420357), because a 1.6 V worst-case V_GS is too large an offset for the HUSB238A undervoltage detector below a 20 V contract.
notes: THIS IS THE UNLABELLED BOX. Hynetek publishes the Figure 6 'Voltage Regulator' with values at https://www.hynetek.com/2730.html - never in the datasheet. It is a BSS138 SOURCE FOLLOWER: gate pulled up through 10 kOhm and clamped by a 28 V Zener, source feeding the HUSB238A VBUS pin. A 0 Ohm link (RJ2 in their reference) bypasses it for builds at 28 V or below.

A source follower, NOT the resistor-plus-Zener shunt assumed earlier. The distinction matters: a follower holds the pin at roughly (Vgate - Vth) with low output impedance, whereas a series resistor would drop voltage with load current.

FOLLOWER DROP RESOLVED, two parts. (1) HUSB238A VDD (pin 5) is an INPUT supply, not an output - p.4 recommends tying it to a 3.3 V rail - which drops the VBUS-pin requirement from 4.5 V to 3.15 V and its draw from 4.5 mA to 800 uA. (2) D14 (RB751V-40, C7502691) from the 5 V rail to the VBUS pin holds it at 4.19 V on a 4.75 V bus. This part's Vgs was never the thing to fix; the pin's requirement was.

Residual at vSafe5V: VBUS_OK rising (vVBPRS_R, 3.67/4.0/4.4 V min/typ/max, p.7) clears the pin by 0.11 V at the converter's applicable R_DS corner (pin 4.11 V) and by 0.19 V on a typical one (pin 4.19 V), and misses by 0.29 V on a max-threshold part. The under-voltage detector publishes no band covering a 5 V RDO: p.7 gives 86% for 26 V > RDO > 10 V (F0) and 80% for 10 V >= RDO > 5 V (F1). The ADJACENT band is F1, which ends exactly at 5 V - F0 starts at 10 V, one band further up - and at 80% the bound is 4.00 V, which the pin clears by 0.11 V at the converter's applicable R_DS corner and 0.19 V on a typical one. Reading F0's 86% instead gives 4.30 V and leaves the pin 0.19 V short at the corner, 0.11 V on a typical converter; that is the pessimistic case, not the adjacent one. The lever if it fails is the 5 V rail, which sits at its own dropout floor, not the diode.

ROLE EXPANDED: also fitted as the FAULT interlock transistors, replacing 2N7002 there. V_GS(th) 1.6 V max (this LCSC part, not the 1.5 V of other vendors) against the 2N7002's 2.5 V means the HUSB238A's 2.64 V V_OH leaves 1.04 V of worst-case overdrive rather than 0.14 V. Same part, same footprint, one fewer line on the BOM.

WHY IT LOST THE FOLLOWER ROLE: the detector compares the VBUS pin against a percentage of the requested voltage, so the pass condition is V_GS <= 0.09*V in the 86% band. 1.6 V needs V >= 17.8 V, which fails 9 V, 12 V and 15 V. It remains correct as a logic-level interlock switch, where the threshold being high is irrelevant - the GPIO drives it at 3.3 V.
